references.text: Direct continuation of the same event: The transition from bartering livestock to purchasing the people and the land.
Complementary phases in Joseph's handling of his brothers: From secret repayment to public barter.
Parallel regarding resource limits: Both texts address the problem of obtaining food when money is no longer sufficient.
The motif 'silver' connects the brothers' fear (v.18) with the economic reality (v.16).
Development of Joseph's strategy: From leaving silver for grain to demanding livestock once the silver was exhausted.
Continuous narrative: From the first cry for bread (v.55) to the changed barter when the money ran out (v.16).
